Title: Connector Onboarding Questionnaire and Schema Contract
Purpose: This document is a practical onboarding questionnaire and binding schema contract for customers integrating Redwood's SIEM export connectors with Splunk, Datadog, and Microsoft Sentinel. It defines the minimum required fields, mapping expectations, delivery semantics, RBAC v2 considerations, and evidence-automation hooks that downstream SOC/Compliance teams will use to validate exports.
Scope:
- Applies to all SIEM export connector projects (hosted and Private deployments).
- Focused on connector-to-SIEM data format, security obligations, and acceptance criteria from a compliance perspective.
- Not a full implementation spec for runtime internals; assumes serving/runtime teams will translate the contract into exporter behavior.
Intended audience:
- Customer security/compliance reps completing onboarding
- Solutions Engineering implementing connector configs
- Infra / Exporter engineers who implement delivery behavior
- Customer Success and SRE teams running validation
Pre-Onboarding Questionnaire (to be fill:
1) Primary contact and backup (name/email/role)
2) Target SIEM product and edition: Splunk Cloud / Splunk Enterprise / Datadog Logs / Datadog SIEM / Microsoft Sentinel (Azure Sentinel)
3) Destination ingestion mechanism: HTTP Event Collector (HEC) / Datadog HTTP API / Azure Event Hubs / Azure Sentinel Data Collector API. Provide endpoint URLs, proxy requirements, and any VNet details.
4) Authentication & key rotation cadence: HEC token rotation schedule, Datadog API key TTL, Azure Managed Identity usage, or customer-provided certs.
5) Expected peak throughput (events/sec) and average event size (bytes) during business hours.
6) Retention and legal hold expectations for exported logs/messages (e.g., 3 years, 7 years). Any special archives required?
7) Required PII redaction policy and per-field sensitivity labels (PII, PHI, PCI, internal-only).
8) Required field canonicalization for incident correlation (user_id, tenant_id, request_id, trace_id) and preferred key names in SIEM.
9) Regulatory evidence requirements (which audit events must be preserved verbatim vs. redacted summaries).
10) SLA/uptime constraints and business impact categories (P0/P1 mapping).
Schema Contract (minimum required envelo:
- export_version: string (semantic, e.g., "1.0")
- timestamp_utc: string (RFC3339)
- provider: string ("redwood-inference")
- customer_tenant_id: string (opaque UUID)
- product_area: string (one of: auth, model_serving, audit, billing, admin)
- event_type: string (short name, e.g., "session.create", "apikey.revoke")
- event_severity: string (info|warning|error|security)
- trace_id: string (optional, if available)
- request_id: string
- user_identifier: string (canonicalized per onboarding Q8)
- rbac_v2_action: string (create|read|update|delete|grant|revoke)
- rbac_v2_resource: string (resource type + id)
- payload: string (json-encoded string of event details OR structured JSON if the destination supports structured fields)
- evidence_reference: string (opaque reference used by evidence-automation subsystem for proofs)
- delivery_metadata: string (json describing attempts, latency_ms, exporter_version)
Mapping guidance per SIEM:
- Splunk: ship NDJSON lines or HEC events. Use index naming convention: redwood_<tenant>_<area>. For structured payloads prefer fields rather than big message blob to enable Splunk search/field extraction. Map timestamp_utc to _time.
- Datadog: send as JSON body to Logs API. Recommend mapping product_area to service, event_type to "dd.tags.event_type" and put rbac_v2 fields as tags for fast correlation. Use user_identifier in "user" facet.
- Sentinel: send to Event Hubs or Data Collector API. Flatten payload fields into properties.* when possible. Ensure timestamp_utc becomes TimeGenerated.
Field mapping examples (canonical keys):
- tenant -> customer_tenant_id
- actor -> user_identifier
- action -> rbac_v2_action
- resource -> rbac_v2_resource
- evidence_id -> evidence_reference
Connector behavior & delivery semantics:
1) At-least-once delivery with exactly-once best-effort: exporters must include delivery_metadata.attempts and a stable request_id for dedup checks on consumer side.
2) Batching: exporters may batch up to X events (customer-specified) or Y KB per payload. Batching must preserve NDJSON line boundaries if using NDJSON mode.
3) Backpressure: if SIEM endpoint returns 429 or connection resets, exporter should implement exponential backoff with jitter and persist to a local durable queue for private deploys. For hosted mode, fallback to a lower-tier ephemeral store and trigger CS notify if queue length exceeds configured threshold.
4) Partial failures: connector must report which events failed in the batch and include per-event delivery error in delivery_metadata for audit.
5) Schema evolution: add-only fields allowed. Removing or renaming existing canonical fields requires a migration RFC and compatibility window of 90 days after announcement.
RBAC v2 and audit constraints:
- All RBAC mutations (grant/revoke) must emit an event with rbac_v2_action and rbac_v2_resource populated and a link to the pre/post-state snapshot in evidence_reference.
- Read operations should emit lower-severity access logs (event_severity=info) including authorized_by and authorization_policy_id where applicable.
- The connector contract enforces retention of immutable audit snapshots for the customer-specified retention period; if the customer requests long-term retention, the connector must include a pointer to the archived evidence store in evidence_reference.
PII & Redaction rules:
- Sensitive fields specified in onboarding Q7 must be either removed, tokenized (deterministic hash with salt), or redacted using replacement value "[REDACTED]" depending on customer preference.
- Hashing algorithm recommendation: HMAC-SHA256 with tenant-scoped key; do not use plain SHA variants without a key.
- Redaction must be reversible only if explicit legal/forensics exceptions are authorized and a KMS-backed reversible tokenization is configured.
Evidence automation hooks:
- evidence_reference must be globally unique and resolve to a stable proof bundle in the evidence automation service (e.g., S3 path or signed URL). Proof bundle includes: raw_event.json, delivery_proof.json (signed timestamped delivery metadata), and integrity_signature (base64).
- For high-assurance events (security/severity=security), the exporter must trigger evidence pipeline ingestion and set evidence_reference to the resulting bundle id.
- Proof bundle metadata must include exporter_version and exporter_config_snapshot for reproducibility.
Acceptance tests and metrics (customer a:
- Test #1: End-to-end NDJSON delivery of 1,000 events with 2 simultaneous tenants, validate 100% events ingested and indexed within 120s.
- Test #2: Simulated 429 from SIEM for 30s and sustained 90s recovery; validate queueing behavior and no data loss.
- Test #3: RBAC mutation roundtrip; verify that pre/post state snapshots are linked by evidence_reference and accessible.
- SLO metrics to validate: median delivery latency, p95 delivery latency, dropped_event_rate (must be 0 for critical events), queue_depth.
Rollout & Versioning:
- Each connector must expose exporter_version semver and export_version in payload.
- Version bumps that change canonical keys require a migration note and 90-day compatibility period.
Operational notes for Solutions Engineer:
- Provide templates for Splunk HEC tokens with minimal scopes and recommend per-tenant index seclusion for high-sensitivity customers.
- For Datadog, recommend using role-based API keys and scoping to log ingest only, with separate keys for metrics/trace ingestion.
- For Sentinel, advise using customer-managed Event Hubs in Private deployments to avoid cross-tenant networking exposure.
FAQ (common onboarding items):
Q: Can we compress batches? A: Yes, connectors may gzip batches but must set Content-Encoding and ensure receiver supports it. Include uncompressed size in delivery_metadata.
Q: How are PII exceptions handled? A: Submit legal exception request; Solutions Eng will enable reversible tokenization with KMS and escalate to Security for approval.
Q: What happens on long-term outages? A: For hosted mode, CS will engage and enable temporary S3 archival; for Private mode, on-prem queue persists until customer resolves connectivity.
